name: Real-source monitoring and useful change detection
purpose: Observe an identified real source on a restart-safe cadence, distinguish a meaningful change from noise, and create one traceable useful response without duplicate alerts or stale-source claims.

preconditions.statement: The monitored source identity and acquisition method are independently resolvable.
Prior and current snapshots are timestamped, hashed, and within the declared freshness policy.
The cadence and deduplication key are durable before observation begins.

canonical_targets.authorization_scope: isolated acceptance ledger and candidate files

success_criteria.statement: The accepted change is supported by identified fresh before-and-current source snapshots rather than a fixture or model assertion.
Exactly one durable candidate is created for the meaningful change and repeated observations remain idempotent.
The resulting candidate explains owner value, source provenance, uncertainty, and why the change is actionable.
A corrupt observation or failed downstream write can restore the previous monitor cursor and candidate state.

unacceptable_outcomes.statement: Fixture, stale, or unidentifiable source data is labeled as a current real-source observation.
The same source change creates duplicate candidates, alerts, or downstream effects.
A heartbeat or unchanged value is promoted as useful work merely to show activity.

intervention_rules.trigger: Source freshness expires or identity cannot be resolved
intervention_rules.response: Do not claim a change; record the source as degraded with retry metadata

intervention_rules.trigger: External source is unavailable after bounded retries
intervention_rules.response: Keep the monitor resumable and continue unrelated journeys

intervention_rules.trigger: Authenticated STOP arrives before candidate creation
intervention_rules.response: Persist the observation cursor and refuse the candidate effect

failure_injections.inject: Return a stale snapshot with a valid-looking content hash
Replay the same changed snapshot twice after a restart
failure_injections.expected_response: One idempotency key yields exactly one candidate record

failure_injections.inject: Crash after source capture and before cursor advancement
failure_injections.expected_response: Recovery reconciles the snapshot and advances the cursor without duplicate effect

requirements: Recover the last durable monitor cursor and source snapshot hashes
Reconcile any candidate created before the crash by idempotency key
Resume cadence without skipping or duplicating the change
Restore the previous monitor cursor when the observation is invalid
Remove only the isolated unaccepted candidate effect while preserving its rejection record
rollback.restoration_target: last valid monitor cursor and accepted candidate set
